messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: us-west-2 gateway 5xx rate spike detected. 5xx >= 8% over 5m, p95 latency 620ms. Paging on-call for incidents channel. Correlating with increased upstream timeouts.
Maya (oncall): On it. Paging Jun and Samir. Is this affecting Dedicated pools or only hosted gateway?
Jun (eng-sre): I can see increased 502/504s at the edge gateway in us-west-2. Backend ML workers show elevated queue times and a few OOM restarts on mlworker-12x. Not all tenants.
Samir (runtime): Confirming: redis cache miss rates jumped ~30% before the spike. KV cache eviction logs show frequent TTL evicts. Could be cascading latency.
Ava (support): We already have 3 customers on chat reporting elevated timeouts for generation calls. They see partial responses + retry loops. Need an ETA for mitigation to share.
Maya (oncall): Quick mitigation plan: 1) Open emergency circuit-breaker to reduce retries at gateway, 2) Reroute a portion of traffic off us-west-2 to eu-central-1 as a temporary fallback, 3) Drain problematic backend instances and scale worker pool. Agree?
Jun (eng-sre): +1. I'll start with circuit breaker config. Pushing a limited rule to gateway to cap retries to 1 and fail fast for 5xx.
Samir (runtime): I'll prepare a cross-region model-variant to accept rerouted traffic. Need a canary at 5% before full shift.
Theo (infra): I'll check capacity in eu-central-1 and us-east-1 for headroom. If eu-central already has 80% multinode utilization we may prefer eu-west.
Maya (oncall): Ava, please update affected customers: "We're rerouting a subset of traffic and applying fail-fast to reduce retries; some requests may be slower but overall error rates should drop. Will update in 15m"
Ava (support): Sending now.
Jun (eng-sre): Applying circuit-breaker rule now:
```
# gateway-ratelimit/circuit-breaker
route: /v1/generate
condition: response_5xx_rate > 0.05
action: set_retry_limit(1); set_fail_fast(true)
```
Jun (eng-sre): Rule deployed (id cb-2026-03-15-001). Monitoring.
deploy-bot: Deploy cb-2026-03-15-001 to gateway-usw2 succeeded (3/3 nodes).
ops-bot: Alert suppression engaged for noisy pageresponses for rule cb-2026-03-15-001.
Maya (oncall): Jun — what's the immediate effect?
Jun (eng-sre): 2 minutes in: 5xx rate dipped from 8.4% -> 6.1%. P95 still high but trending down. Some request fanout reduced.
Samir (runtime): Preparing reroute playbook. Command to start a 5% traffic shift to eu-central-1:
```
POST /control/traffic-shift
{ "from": "us-west-2", "to": "eu-central-1", "percent": 5 }
```
Samir (runtime): Ready to trigger after Jun confirms gateway health.
Jun (eng-sre): Gateway health checks backstable. Approve 5% canary.
Maya (oncall): Go ahead. Samir, keep canary for 10 minutes and watch model latency/5xx.
Samir (runtime): Triggered canary. Canaries running: 5% -> eu-central-1. Will print logs here.
Samir (runtime): Canary logs: endpoint /v1/generate — p50 210ms, p95 330ms, 5xx 0.9% on eu-central-1. No model errors.
Jun (eng-sre): In us-west-2, after CB and canary: 5xx now 4.2% and trending down. Looks promising.
Maya (oncall): Increase to 20% if stable for 10m. Also start draining mlworker-12x instance set and spin new workers.
Theo (infra): Draining mlworker-12x group: issuing graceful-drain then terminate. New autoscaled replicas coming up (target +40%).
Theo (infra): Command run: `aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name mlworkers-usw2-asg --desired-capacity 48`
deploy-bot: New worker instances launched; health checks passing (6/6).
Samir (runtime): Noting a correlated spike of redis latency during 5xx window. Will instrument and increase connection pool.
Jun (eng-sre): Checkpoint — customer impact reduced per monitoring and support reports. But we should keep partial fallback in place until we confirm the root cause.
Ava (support): Customers updated: "We've rerouted part of your traffic and applied mitigations. You may see improved stability within 15 minutes. We'll follow up with incident summary"
Maya (oncall): Observability update: synthetic traffic to us-west-2 shows p95 down to 180ms, 5xx steady at 1.8%. EU canary healthy. Rolling traffic shift to 20% now.
Samir (runtime): Increasing cache connection pool and reducing TTL churn. Patch pushed: `cache.max_connections=500` and `cache.eviction_threshold=0.85`.
Jun (eng-sre): Monitoring for flapping — looking at request fanout and retry pileups. No other regions showing similar spikes.
Maya (oncall): OK team: short-term mitigation done. Next actions: 1) Full diagnostic for cache eviction cause (Samir + Theo), 2) Postmortem to include timeline & customer impact (Maya + Ava), 3) Consider automatic regional spillover policy in case of cache-induced gateway spikes (Jun + product).
Samir (runtime): Noted. I'll pull heap dumps from mlworker-12x, review cache eviction logs, and check compaction job timings.
Theo (infra): I'll gather infra metrics (disk, NIC errors) and check instance replacement history.
Ava (support): I'll collect customer request IDs and churn rates for a post-incident report.
Maya (oncall): Moving to incident:monitoring for 45 more minutes. If stable, we'll close the incident and open a postmortem ticket.
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigation in place, severity downgraded to SEV-3. Please file postmortem at /incidents/postmortems/1768736452.
Maya (oncall): Thanks everyone. If anything regresses, ping @oncall immediately. Closing here in 45m unless noise. :white_check_mark:
Jun (eng-sre): One quick note — we should add a temporary canary-route in the gateway to avoid hitting the same cache shard hot keys during recovery. Filing a quick follow-up task.
Samir (runtime): Agreed. Will add sticky hashing fallback for 30m.
Ava (support): Final customer note queued for 20:00 UTC with root cause (once determined).
Maya (oncall): End of thread updates will be added to the postmortem. Good work team.
